No distinct spots, no powdery coating, no gray mold. This suggests a systemic/vascular disease or virus. Top candidates: Verticillium Wilt, Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus, Cucumber Mosaic Virus, Leaf Mold.

All three Leaf Mold references match the test image well - same background, same yellowing pattern. Now I need to cover remaining classes. Let me check Early_Blight, Powdery_Mildew, Septoria, and others.

I've now covered 16 different classes. Based on my analysis:

- **Leaf Mold** references (CDDM_1006, 1036, 1057) all show tomato leaves on gray/neutral backgrounds with the same interveinal yellowing/chlorotic mottling pattern as the test image. Same setting, same color pattern, same leaf shape.
- All other classes showed clearly different features: dark spots (Septoria, Early Blight), fruit lesions (Anthracnose, Bacterial Speck), microscopic images (Gray Mold, Late Blight, Alternaria), bacterial ooze tests (Bacterial Wilt, Southern Bacterial Wilt), purple spots (TSWV), powdery coating (Powdery Mildew), or severe browning (Bacterial Canker, Early Blight).

The test image matches Leaf Mold most closely: green tomato leaf with patchy interveinal yellowing, laid on a gray surface, no discrete spots or mold growth visible on this side.
